text:
Maria R.: Heads-up — got an automated alert from incident-bot for elevated 95th pct tail latency in us-west on text-gen route. Not impacting errors, just latency.
incident-bot: ALERT SEV2: text-gen.us-west - 95p latency 2.3s (threshold 1.2s). Recent deploy: 3287651200.
Lia (oncall): On it, I'm primary for evening. Checking dashboard, looks like a gradual ramp since 21:10 UTC. Any rolling deploys from infra?
Samir P.: I just finished a small config tweak to batching defaults in canary earlier but that was in us-east only. No west deploys from me.
Kevin L.: I ran a quick query — CPU on the model instances is fine, but queue depth has spiked on two hosts. Might be batching/backpressure interaction with the recent kernel change.
Jess T.: If queue depth spike, we should consider short-circuiting batching to reduce head-of-line. Lia, do you want me to flip the low-risk flag to 0.5s TTL on prefix cache?
Lia (oncall): Good idea. Before we change anything, can we confirm customer impact? Are requests timing out or just slower?
Maria R.: No 5xxs in the last 30m. Affected traces show extra waiting time in the batch scheduler. Customer impact: several high-traffic tenants report slow completions (chat UX stutters). Not service-outage but noticeable.
Samir P.: Runbook pointer — see runbook section "batching regression mitigation". Quick excerpt: ```1) set BATCH_MAX_WAIT_MS=5 2) disable continuous batching for route text-gen 3) monitor 95p for 10m 4) escalate if >=2.0s persist``` Link: https://redwood/runbooks/batching-regressions
Lia (oncall): I'm going to try step 1 (tighten BATCH_MAX_WAIT_MS) on the canary group in us-west. Jess, hold off on cache TTL until we see effect. Kevin, can you prepare the rollback candidate if kernel change is culprit?
Kevin L.: Copy. Preparing rollback image and note of hosts to drain. ETA 6m.
Jess T.: Got it. I'll stand by to adjust routing if needed.
incident-bot: NOTE: Pager threshold rules: SEV2 -> page primary oncall immediately; if no ack in 5m, page secondary. Use `@pager` for paging.
Lia (oncall): Acknowledging. Lia (oncall) is primary. Paging secondary if no ack in 5m.
Maria R.: Lia, after you make the canary change, can you post the exact command you ran and the canary ids? We need audit in thread.
Lia (oncall): Ran: ```kubectl set env deployment/text-gen-batch-canary BATCH_MAX_WAIT_MS=5 -n inference-us-west``` Canary IDs: tg-canary-7a3b, tg-canary-7a3c. Monitoring now.
Samir P.: Observing 95p drop to 1.1s on canary hosts — good sign. Please watch for error regression.
Kevin L.: I still have rollback ready but holding. If after 10m 95p remains <=1.2s, we can promote change to blue and then full rollout.
Jess T.: Noted. Reminder on escalation: if 95p > 2.0s OR error rate >0.5% for 10m, page SRE lead (@Kevin L.) and product oncall (@Maria R.). For immediate customer-facing incidents (>=10% tenant requests affected), escalate to oncall manager.
Lia (oncall): After 8m, canary performance stable at 1.05s. Rolling the change to 30% of us-west nodes. Command: ```kubectl rollout restart deployment/text-gen -n inference-us-west --selector=canary=true --timeout=3m```
Maria R.: From comms POV, since no 5xxs and a quick mitigation, we will wait to notify customers. If anything degrades, ping me and I'll prepare a status blurb.
incident-bot: RESOLUTION CHECKPOINT: Please fill incident form if mitigation >30m or if customer-visible impact persists. Link: https://redwood/incidents/new
Lia (oncall): Rolling to 30% done, metrics holding. I'll continue monitoring for 30m. If it reappears or queue depth resurfaces, escalate per runbook: page SRE lead, then infra eng rotation, then exec oncall.
Samir P.: One postmortem note: follow-up to validate kernel scheduler tweak with perf team. I'll open an issue and tag infra-rt.
Jess T.: Quick checklist for future handoffs — leave canary ids, exact env vars changed, metric snapshots (pre/post), and any rollback commands. Put them in the shift-handoff doc under today.
Lia (oncall): Will do. Closing this thread if metrics stable for next 30m, otherwise I'll update. :thumbsup:
